Music driver, called once per frame from the raster interrupt handler at $30E5 ($3111). Zero page $FF is the song requested by the game (0-4). 0: volume to 0 and return, the sequencer frozen. A new number: start that song (music_start_song) and return. The same number as music_current_song: restore volume and filter from their shadows and play one frame (music_play_frame). The game sets $FF to 1 at $1CF8, 2 at $1BE5, 3 at $1B31, 4 at $1764, 0 at $18ED.

Start song A: record it in music_current_song, clear the SID and the filter state (music_sid_clear), reset the three voices, mark them active ($81), set the volume from song_volume_table and every tempo counter from song_tempo_table, then copy the song base, the pattern-offset table address (into the operands at $0AD1 and $0ADD) and the three order-list pointers from the song tables indexed by song*2.

One frame of music, voices 3 to 1: count down each active voice tempo counter and, when it expires, run one sequencer tick through the order-list command at music_order_index (music_order_dispatch). Every frame each voice then glides or sets its pitch (music_voice_pitch); after the loop the LFOs, pulse widths and filter sweep are updated and the active voices are written to the SID (Y = 14, 7, 0, the voice register offsets).
Read the command byte at music_order_index in the voice order list ($F9/$FA) and jump through music_order_commands ($FD/$FE), with Y = the order index. X = voice.

Per frame pitch of voice X: if the instrument has a slide (music_slide_enable) step the SID frequency toward the target (music_pitch_slide); otherwise copy the target frequency straight to it. Then on to the next voice.

Order-list command 1, n: play pattern n. On the first tick (music_pattern_start_flag set) look up the pattern address (song base + offset table entry, through operands written at song start), clear the flag and read the first event. Afterwards count down the note timer: at 0 a release tick (gate off unless tied), then the next pattern event. Pattern events: $FF ends the pattern (order index += 2, next command at once); $80+n selects instrument n (music_select_instrument); a note byte and length byte set the target frequency, timer, flags and gate.
Operand of LDA $0973,Y at $0AD0: the low byte of the current song pattern-offset table address, written by music_start_song ($0A18).
Operand high byte for $0AD0, written by music_start_song ($0A21).
Operand of LDA $0974,Y at $0ADC: the offset table address plus 1, written by music_start_song ($0A15, then incremented at $0A24).
Operand high byte for $0ADC, written at $0A1E and carried into at $0A29.

Part of a note start: unless the previous note asked for a glide or tie (music_note_flags), the SID frequency jumps to the new target; then the new flags are stored and the gate is set for a note other than a rest.
Copy voice X shadows to the SID at $D400+Y (Y = 0, 7 or 14): frequency, pulse width, attack/decay, sustain/release, then the control register last.
Zero the SID registers $D400-$D418 (silence, volume 0) and the filter shadows: route and mode/volume 0, sweep shift and direction 0, cutoff base $6400.

Reset voice X: inactive, repeat counter, order index, transpose, flags, control, LFO value, rate and direction, pulse base and width, slide 0; pattern-start flag and tempo counter 1; no PWM source ($80). Also turns the filter sweep off (music_filter_mod_source = $80). Order-list command 0 and song start use it.
Reset all three voices with music_voice_reset (X = 2, 1, 0).
Order-list command 2, i: continue this voice order list at index i (music_order_index = i) and dispatch it at once. Used to loop a song.
Order-list command 0: stop this voice (music_voice_reset makes it inactive, so the SID registers are no longer written for it). Only song 4 uses it; songs 1-3 loop.

Order-list command 3, i, c: the first time, set the voice repeat counter to c and go to index i; each later time count down and go to i again until the counter reaches 0, then skip the three bytes and carry on.
Per voice (3 bytes, X = 0-2): low byte of the target SID frequency of the current note: music_note_freq_table entry shifted left by the octave. Written at $0B4D, read by music_pitch_slide and $0A99.
Per voice: high byte of the target frequency (starts at 1 and is shifted left with the low byte, $0B52-$0B69).
Per voice: low byte of the pulse width set by a pulse instrument (instrument bytes 1-2); music_pwm_update adds the modulation to it.
Per voice: high byte of the base pulse width.
Per voice: shadow of the SID control register (waveform bits from the instrument, bit 0 gate). Gate is set when a note starts ($0BAD) and cleared on the release tick ($0B13).
Per voice: attack/decay from the instrument, written to $D405+voice offset.
Per voice: sustain/release from the instrument, written to $D406+voice offset.
Voice 1 active flag. $81 after a song starts ($09DC); 0 after an order-list stop command. Bit 7 set means the voice is played and its registers are copied to the SID each frame ($0AB5).
Voice 2 active flag, as music_voice_active.
Voice 3 active flag, as music_voice_active.
Voice 1 order-list pointer, low byte, from song_orders_v1 at song start; loaded into $F9 each tick. The next two bytes are voices 2 and 3.
Voice 2 order-list pointer, low byte (from the voice 2 table at $0F72).
Voice 3 order-list pointer, low byte (from the voice 3 table at $0F7C).
Voice 1 order-list pointer, high byte; loaded into $FA each tick.
Voice 2 order-list pointer, high byte.
Voice 3 order-list pointer, high byte.
Per voice: low byte of the address of the pattern being played (song base + offset, $0AD7); loaded into $FB each tick.
Per voice: high byte of the pattern address; loaded into $FC.
Per voice: index of the current command in the voice order list (advanced by 2 after a pattern, set by jump and repeat commands).
Per voice: 1 when the next tick must take a new pattern number from the order list (set at song start and at a pattern end marker $FF), 0 while a pattern plays.
Per voice: offset of the next byte to read in the current pattern.
Per voice: ticks left in the current note (from music_duration_table), then 1 for the release tick.
Per voice: 0 while the note sounds; nonzero during the release tick, after which the next note is read. A length index of 14 sets it at once, so that note has no release tick.
Per voice: octave offset from the instrument (its transpose byte), added to the octave field of each note ($0B5D).
Filter cutoff base, low byte (shared): from a filtered instrument, or 0 at song start; the filter sweep adds to it.
Filter cutoff base, high byte; $64 at song start ($0BF7).
Index (0-4) into music_lfo_value of the value that sweeps the filter cutoff; bit 7 set (as at song start) means no sweep.
Number of left shifts applied to the filter sweep value before it is added to or taken from the cutoff.
Filter sweep direction: 0 adds the modulation to the cutoff base, anything else subtracts it ($0E8B).

Per voice: bits 6-7 of the current note length byte. Bit 6 keeps the gate on at the note end (tie). Either bit stops the next note from jumping to its pitch ($0B8C), so with a slide rate it glides there from this one.
Per voice: octave of the current note (note bits 4-6 + transpose); the number of left shifts of the base frequency and of the slide step.
Per voice: semitone of the current note, 1-12, or 0 for a rest (no gate).
Voice 1 tempo counter: counts frames down to the next sequencer tick, reloaded from music_tempo_reload.
Voice 2 tempo counter (set with the others from song_tempo_table at $09F7).
Voice 3 tempo counter.
Voice 1 frames per tick, from song_tempo_table (1 or 2).
Voice 2 frames per tick.
Voice 3 frames per tick.
Scratch: high byte of a shifted modulation or slide step in the PWM, filter and slide routines.
Scratch: low byte of the slide step in the downward pitch slide ($0F1F). $0CD8-$0CDA after it are not referenced.
Five modulation sources indexed 0-4: three triangle LFOs (0-2, one per voice, ramping between 0 and $FF), then the SID voice 3 envelope (3) and oscillator (4) sampled each frame.
Modulation source 3: $D41C (voice 3 envelope output), copied each frame by music_lfo_update.
Modulation source 4: $D41B (voice 3 oscillator output), copied each frame.
Per LFO: step added or taken each frame; set from byte 5 of a pulse instrument.
Per LFO: 0 rising, $FF falling; flips when the value reaches $FF or 0.
Per voice: modulation source for the pulse width, the voice own LFO, or bit 7 set for none (instrument byte 3, $0D6D).
Per voice: left shifts applied to the LFO value before it is added to the pulse width.
Per voice: pulse width written to the SID, low byte (base + modulation).
Per voice: pulse width written to the SID, high byte.
Per voice: frequency written to the SID, low byte; follows the target directly or by a slide.
Per voice: frequency written to the SID, high byte.
Per voice: nonzero when the instrument has a slide rate; music_pitch_slide then moves the frequency to the target instead of jumping.
Per voice: slide step, low byte (instrument byte), shifted left by the octave.
Per voice: slide step, high byte. Only ever zeroed (voice reset), so the step is the low byte shifted.
Per voice: passes left for the order-list repeat command; 0 when no repeat is in progress.
Eight AND masks $FE $FD ... $7F that clear bit n; the driver uses entries 0-2 to take voice n out of the filter ($0DF2).
Eight OR masks $01 ... $80 that set bit n; the driver uses entries 0-2 to route voice n through the filter ($0DA2).

SID frequency low bytes of the twelve semitones of the lowest octave, indexed 1-12 (entry 0 unused, rests never read it); the high byte is always 1 ($10C-$1FA). They are C to B tuned for the NTSC clock (within 5 cents), so on PAL every note sounds about 66 cents flat.

Note lengths in ticks, indexed by bits 0-3 of the length byte: 2 5 8 11 17 23 35 47 71 1 3 7 6 4 1 1. A note lasts the value plus one release tick (3, 6, 9, 12, 18, 24, 36, 48, 72 ...), except index 14, which has no release tick.

Order-list command handlers, by command byte: 0 music_cmd_stop $0C58, 1 music_cmd_play_pattern $0AC6, 2 music_cmd_jump $0C4F, 3 music_cmd_repeat $0C5E. Read at $0A7E and entered by JMP ($FD) at $0A8B.
High byte of entry 0 of music_order_commands, named because $0A83 reads it as music_order_commands+1,Y.
Shadow of $D418: low nibble volume from song_volume_table, high nibble filter mode from a filtered instrument. Rewritten to the SID every frame a song plays.
Song the driver is playing (1-4). music_play compares $FF with it to see a new request. Not cleared when $FF is 0.
Shadow of $D417: low bits the voices routed through the filter, high nibble resonance from a filtered instrument.

Load instrument A (pattern byte $80+n) on voice X from music_instrument_table: waveform into the control shadow keeping the gate bit; for a pulse waveform ($40 exactly) the pulse width, PWM source, shift and the voice LFO rate; then AD, SR, slide rate, transpose; and if the filter flag is set, route the voice through the filter and set filter mode, resonance, cutoff base and sweep (written to $D415-$D418 at once), else take the voice out of the filter.

Once per frame: sample the voice 3 envelope ($D41C) and oscillator ($D41B) as modulation sources 3 and 4, then move each of the three triangle LFOs by its rate, up to $FF and down to 0, reversing at each end.
Once per frame, each voice with a PWM source: pulse width = base + (source value shifted left by the PWM shift), 16 bits.
Once per frame unless the sweep is off (bit 7 of music_filter_mod_source): cutoff = base plus or minus the source value shifted left by music_filter_mod_shift, written to $D415/$D416.
Move the SID frequency of voice X toward its target by the slide rate shifted left by the note octave, upward ($0EC8) or downward ($0F0A), stopping exactly on the target.
Base address of the current song patterns, copied from song_base_table when the song starts ($0A09); added to every pattern offset ($0AD4).
High byte of music_song_base, written at $0A0F and added at $0ADF.

High bytes of song_offsets_table, read as $0F5F,Y at $0A1B.

High bytes of song_orders_v2, read at $0A3E.

Per-move table, 25 bytes indexed by a fighter's move number ($61,X, moves $00-$18): what happens at the end of the move's animation. Read at $2A70 and $2ACD. $80 (moves 2 and 3, walking forward and back): the move is replaced at once by the requested move ($63,X; $11 becomes $12). 1 (moves 0, 1, 5, 8, 9, $0E, $16, $17): the fighter goes back to move 1 (standing) when it ends. 0 (the rest, the blows among them): the fighter holds the last frame ($74,X set at $2AD4) and the animation then runs backwards ($4B,X).

Per-move table, 25 bytes: 1 for the eleven moves that can score, 0 otherwise. The blows are 6, 7 (the two diagonal-forward moves without fire), $0A-$11 (the eight directions with fire) and $18 (move 7 begun from a stance other than 4 or 7, $2B41). Read by the computer opponent ($22FA: is the other fighter attacking), the blocking code ($2B1D), the move start ($2B4F: a blow starts sound $3164), hit detection ($2B72: only a blow is tested) and $2827.

Per-move table, 25 bytes: the move that defends against each blow. $14 against 6, $0D, $0E, $0F, $11; $13 against 7, $0B, $0C, $18; 5 (the jump, joystick up) against $0A and $10; 0 for moves that are not blows. A player pulling back (requested move 3) while the opponent's blow is in range ($2D00) gets this move instead ($2B2D), and the computer opponent picks it too ($2309, $23B5).

Per-move table, 21 bytes (moves $15-$18 read on into move_full_window, all zero there): non-zero for moves 3, 9, $0F and $10. For the blows $0F and $10 the hit test ($2BE6, $2C71, $2CC4, ...) measures the distance the other way: the opponent must be at or beyond the reach instead of at or inside it.

Per-move table, 25 bytes: how far inside a blow's reach the opponent may stand and still be hit for a whole point (yin-yang). The hit test at $2BF4/$2C0D/$2C7E/$2C97 compares the distance between the fighters with the reach read for the opponent's current frame: equal, or short of it by up to this many units, scores 2 in $6E,X. Values 1-4; zero for moves that are not blows.

Per-move table, 25 bytes: the wider margin inside a blow's reach that still scores a half point (1 in $6E,X), tested after move_full_window at $2BFD/$2C16/$2C87/$2CA0. Values 5-$0A. An opponent closer than this is not hit at all.

21 bytes laid out like a per-move table (1 at offsets 7, $0A, $0B, $0C and $11, all blow numbers; 0 elsewhere) that no instruction was found to read: the readers of move_half_window use indices up to $18 only, ending at $11EE. Purpose not known.

Per-move table, 25 bytes: the animation frame ($51,X) on which a blow is tested for a hit (compared at $2B83): move 6 frame 7, 7 $0D, $0A $10, $0B 8, $0C 5, $0D $0B, $0E $0A, $0F $12, $10 $39, $11 $24, $18 $13; 0 for moves that are not blows.

Per-move word table (25 words, $121D-$124E): for each blow, the address of a reach table ($7200-$744E) indexed by the opponent's animation frame ($51 of the other fighter); a byte there is the reach in that frame, $80 meaning that frame cannot be hit. Used by $2B9B when the fighters face opposite ways ($53 differs). Zero for moves that are not blows.
High-byte view of move_reach_ptr_facing: $2BA0 reads the second byte of each word here with the move number doubled.

Per-move word table (25 words, $124F-$1280): the reach table for each blow ($7489-$76D7) used by $2BAC when both fighters face the same way, so the blow lands on the opponent's back; tested at $2C44 with the distance taken the other way round.
High-byte view of move_reach_ptr_same_facing, read by $2BB1.

Twelve words that no instruction was found to read: $E640 (the first byte of the backdrop bitmap that bitmap_unpack fills), $3600, $4500, $5400, $6300, then $64E0 to $7020 in steps of $1E0 (480 bytes, twelve 40-byte rows). Possibly a leftover; purpose not known.

The one-player high score, six screen codes ('     0' in the image: blanks then a digit, same format as the scores on screen). Shown at $CCB1 (row 4, columns 17-22) by $2115 when $AE = 0; raised by hiscore_update ($200A) when player 1's score ($CC31) beats it.
The two-player high score, six screen codes in the same format as hiscore_1p; shown at $CCB1 by $2115 when $AE is not 0, and raised by $200A from either player's score ($CC31 or $CC41).

Per-move table, 25 bytes: the points a blow earns, in hundreds. $206C reads it with the scoring move in $8C and adds that many hundreds to the score on screen; a half point ($6E/$6F not 2) earns half (LSR, rounded down). Move 6: 800, 7: 800, $0A: 400, $0B: 200, $0C: 200, $0D: 800, $0E: 1000, $0F: 800, $10: 800, $11: 1000, $18: 600. $2169 adds the same value (halved likewise) to the fighter's total in $BD,X.
'1 PLAYER', eight screen codes (ASCII order in this font), copied to $CCBF (row 4, columns 31-38) by $2186 when $AE = 0.
'2 PLAYER', eight screen codes, copied to $CCBF by $2186 when $AE = 1.

Two bytes, one per fighter: the column offset of that fighter's yin-yang symbols on the top rows, 0 for fighter 0 (columns 3-4) and $1D for fighter 1 (columns 32-33). Passed in Y to $1DDE (whole symbol, characters $21-$24) or $1DF3 (characters $25-$28) by the hit test at $2C28/$2C3B, only in a two-player game ($AE = 1).

Per-move table, 25 bytes, read by $2698 (computer opponent): when the other fighter's move is 4, 7, $0A or $10 (low moves), the move the computer had chosen is swapped for this entry. Mostly the identity; blows map to $0A (moves 7, $0C, $0E, $11), $0B (6, $0D, $18) or $10 ($0F, $10).

Two bytes, indexed by a fighter's facing ($53,X): the smallest X position ($6A,X) allowed, $0C facing one way and 0 the other. Clamped at $3858; a position of $C8 or more counts as below the minimum (wrapped past zero).
Two bytes, indexed by facing ($53,X): the largest X position allowed, $95 and $89. Clamped at $3862 in the same routine as x_min_by_facing (only while the animation frame $51,X is below $3B).
Sets zero page $02-$13 to 0. No JSR, JMP or pointer to $12ED was found in the image; it decodes cleanly and ends in RTS, so it is probably code that nothing calls.

Bonus round, one frame of the player (fighter 0): $5D = 0, read the controls or forced move ($2834), turn a request for move 7 into $18 ($2B33), then $29B4, start or continue the move ($2B46) and handle the end of its animation ($2A8F). Unlike a bout's fighter step ($2808) there is no hit test and no automatic block. Called from bull_round while the player is still up ($5E = 0).
Bonus round set-up of fighter 0: X position $6A = $3E, $6C = $50, facing $53 = 0, clears $4B, $74, $47, sets $45 = 1 and move $61 = 1 (standing), then one animation step ($37BD, X = 0).

The bonus round: a charging bull played by fighter slot 1. Called from the one-player game ($1C24) after a stage won on backdrop 3 ($AF & 3 = 3). Sprites 0-5 on, places the player (bull_round_place_player), puts the bull at X $6B = $B0 with animation $46 = $1C, and runs one pass per frame (waits for raster $FD). The bull is felled ($C2 = $80, animation $1D, 3000 points to player 1: thirty calls of $2095 with X = 9) when the player's frame $51 is $0D, the frame flag $88 is set and the bull is 25-29 units ahead ($6B - $6A in $19-$1D); frame $0D is move 7's strike frame (move_strike_frame), so in effect only that blow works. Otherwise the bull hits the player ($5F = $16, sound $315E, $C2 = 1) when its distance is no more than bull_hit_reach[$51]. Loops while bull_round_bull_step returns non-zero.

Bonus round, one frame of the bull (fighter slot 1, $5D = $40): animation step ($37BD, X = 1). Once felled ($C2 negative) it returns $5A EOR 1, ending the round when that animation completes. While charging, at the end of each animation cycle ($5A set) it reads the bull's X position $6B: 0 sets it to $0C with animation $1E, 2 sets $0E with $1F, 1 ends the round (A = 0), adding 500 points (five calls of $2095) if the player is neither hit ($5F) nor down ($5E); any other position continues the charge (animation $1C, sound $316A while $33 is non-zero). Returns A = 1 to continue.

Bonus round, 59 bytes indexed by the player's animation frame $51 ($00-$3A): how close the bull must come to hit the player in that frame, compared with $6B - $6A at $13AA. $80 means the bull cannot hit the player in that frame (frames $0A, $14-$17, $20-$21, $25-$2F, $35-$38 and $3A). Only read while the bull is not behind the player ($6B >= $6A)..

End of a one-player game (called from $1F0D): enters player 1's score into the five-place high-score table (hiscore_insert), then, unless fire on joystick port 2 is held ($DC00 bit 4 low: return at once, which leaves an entered name as '......'), shows the table. If the score made the table ($CB = 0-4): draws it, points the self-modified store at $17AF to the name's screen cells ($CC13 + 40 x $CB) and $CC/$CD to its colour RAM row ($D808 + 40 x $CB), colours that row 0, lets the player type a name (hiscore_type_name), then colours the row 6. If not ($CB = 5): draws the table and waits up to 250 frames, ending early on fire (port 2) or F1 (row 0, column 4).

Scans the keyboard matrix itself, rows 7 down to 0 (row select from kbd_row_select into $DC00, columns read from $DC01), ignoring the keys set in kbd_ignore_mask. Returns A = 8 x row + column of the first key found (in a row, the highest column first), or $40 when none; uses $C4. Sets $DC02 = $FF and $DC03 = 0.
Eight values for $DC00, one bit low each: $FE selects keyboard row 0 ... $7F row 7. Indexed by the row number in keyboard_scan.
Eight bytes, 8 x row (0, 8, ... $38), the first code of each keyboard row; keyboard_scan ORs in the column.

Eight bytes ORed into each row's column bits by keyboard_scan, so a set bit hides that key: row 0 $FC (only DEL and RETURN kept), row 1 $80 (left SHIFT), row 5 $F9 (only P and L), row 6 $FF (all), row 7 $A6 (only 1, 2, SPACE and Q). Rows 2-4 are read whole. What is left is the letters, the digits, SPACE, DEL and RETURN.

Reads one key for name entry: keyboard_scan, then translates the code through key_ascii. Returns $40 when no key is down, and also while the same key is still held (the last key is kept in $C7), so a held key types once. Otherwise returns the character (ASCII order, which this font follows) and stores it in $C7.

64 bytes, the character for each key code 8 x row + column, in the C64 matrix order: row 0 DEL $14, RETURN $0D, CRSR right $1D, F7 $88, F1 $85, F3 $86, F5 $87, CRSR down $11; row 1 '3WA4ZSE' and 0 for SHIFT; row 2 '5RD6CFTX'; row 3 '7YG8BHUV'; row 4 '9IJ0MKON'; row 5 0, 'PL-.:@,'; row 6 '&*;', $13, 0, '=', $7E, '/'; row 7 '1', 0, 0, '2', SPACE, 0, 'Q', 0. Used only by key_read_new for typing a high-score name; the fight's keyboard controls are read elsewhere ($288C).

Draws the high-score table on the five text rows at the top: clears them (clear_top_rows), puts the places '1'-'5' in column 8 of rows 0-4 ($CC08, $CC30, ...), and for each entry 4 down to 0 whose hiscore_ranks byte is not negative prints the rank reached ($21FB with $CA = 1, in columns 10-18 of the entry's row; $BF/$C0 walk up from $CCAA). Names and scores are drawn by the callers (hiscore_draw_names, hiscore_draw_scores). Uses $C8, $CA, $BF/$C0.

Copies a 30-byte column of the high-score table (five 6-byte fields) to the screen, entry 4 at the row ($BF/$C0) given and each earlier entry one row (40 bytes) higher. The source is the operand of the LDA at $15F5, written by its callers ($1618/$161D, $162E/$1633). Leaves $BF/$C0 40 bytes above row 0.
Low byte of the LDA operand at $15F5, the table hiscore_copy_column reads: written by $1616 ($15, names at $1715) and $162C ($33, scores at $1733).
High byte of the LDA operand at $15F5, written as $17 by $161B and $1631; the image holds $80 (the assembled placeholder $8000).
Draws the five names (hiscore_names, $1715) at columns 19-24 of rows 0-4: patches hiscore_copy_column's source to $1715 and starts it at $CCB3.
Draws the five scores (hiscore_scores, $1733) at columns 26-31 of rows 0-4: patches hiscore_copy_column's source to $1733 and starts it at $CCBA.

Finds player 1's place in the high-score table and makes room for it. Compares the score on screen ($CC31, six digits; $2049 with X = 9) with the stored scores from the fifth up; the place $CB is 0-4 above the first entry that is equal or higher, 5 when the score does not beat the fifth (nothing changes then; a tie never enters). Otherwise shifts the lower names, scores and ranks down one (hiscore_shift_names, hiscore_shift_scores, hiscore_insert_rank, which stores $C9), copies the score in ($205E) and blanks the name to '......' (hiscore_blank_name). Leaves $BF/$C0 pointing at the name.
Moves the names at and below place Y (0-3) down one place, the fifth name dropping out: name 4 = name 3 always, then 3 = 2 if Y < 3, 2 = 1 if Y < 2, 1 = 0 if Y = 0. Six bytes each, X = 5 down to 0.
Moves the scores at and below place Y (0-3) down one place, the same way hiscore_shift_names moves the names, in hiscore_scores ($1733-$1750).
Fills the first five text rows, screen $CC00-$CCC7 (200 bytes), with spaces. Called by hiscore_draw and after the high-score screen ($1F10).
Stores the rank $C9 (0 novice, 1-10 dan) for the new entry at place Y in hiscore_ranks, moving the entries from Y to 3 down one first; at place 4 it just stores. Keeps $C8 = Y.

The high-score names: five 6-byte fields, first place at $1715, then $171B, $1721, $1727, $172D; '......' (six $2E) in the image, as the disk holds them. Written by hiscore_shift_names, hiscore_blank_name and hiscore_type_name; drawn by hiscore_draw_names.
Second-place name (six characters), inside hiscore_names.
Third-place name, inside hiscore_names.
Fourth-place name, inside hiscore_names.
Fifth-place name, inside hiscore_names: the one dropped when a new score enters.

The high scores: five 6-byte fields in screen-code digits with leading spaces, first place at $1733, then $1739, $173F, $1745, $174B; all '     0' in the image. Compared and written by hiscore_insert, shifted by hiscore_shift_scores, drawn by hiscore_draw_scores.
Second-place score (six screen codes), inside hiscore_scores.
Third-place score, inside hiscore_scores.
Fourth-place score, inside hiscore_scores.
Fifth-place score, inside hiscore_scores; hiscore_insert starts its comparison here.
The rank reached for each of the five high-score entries: 0 novice, 1-10 dan, $80 (all five in the image) for an empty place, which hiscore_draw leaves blank. Written by hiscore_insert_rank from $C9.
Ranks of places 2-5, inside hiscore_ranks; hiscore_insert_rank shifts them by storing here ($1704).
Writes six '.' ($2E) at ($BF/$C0): the new entry's name before it is typed.

Lets the player type a name of up to six characters into the entry at ($BF), echoed on screen through hiscore_put_char. Sets $FF = 4 (song 4). Each pass waits two frames ($21CA, X = 1, Y = 2) and reads a key (key_read_new). DEL ($14) steps back and blanks a character (not past the first); RETURN, or fire on joystick port 2, fills the rest with spaces and ends; any other character is stored and the sixth ends the entry. Uses $73 for the position.
Stores A at ($BF),Y (the name in the table) and on screen; the screen address is the operand of the STA at $17AF, written by hiscore_after_game ($149C, $14AA, $14B0) as $CC13 + 40 x place.
Low byte of the STA $CC00,Y operand at $17AF: the screen address of the name being typed, $13 + 40 x place, written by hiscore_after_game at $14B0.
High byte of the STA operand at $17AF: $CC plus the carry of the place multiplication, written at $149C and $14AA.
Fills 24 colour RAM cells from ($CC/$CD) with A: the high-score row being typed (columns 8-31).

Unpacks the backdrop for stage $AF & 3 into the bitmap: takes the backdrop's packed stream address from the word table at $1839, adds the stream's first word (the offset to its last byte) and reads backwards from there, writing downwards from $F53F. Control byte n < $80: copy the n bytes below it; n >= $80: repeat the byte below it n & $7F times; 0 ends. Pointers in $34/$35 (source), $36/$37 (destination), count in $38; uses $181D and $182B to step them. Called by $1F54 when the stage's backdrop changes.

Run branch of the backdrop bitmap unpacker that starts at $17BB: control byte with bit 7 set = a run of (byte AND $7F) copies of the byte before it in the stream. Moves the source pointer $34/$35 back two bytes ($182B with $38 = 1), the destination $36/$37 back by the count ($181D), fills downwards with STA ($36),Y, then returns to the control-byte loop at $17E5. $181C is the unpacker's exit on a zero control byte.
Backdrop unpacker helper: destination pointer $36/$37 minus the count in $38 (16-bit). The bitmap is rebuilt from its end ($F53F) towards its start.

Backdrop unpacker helper: source pointer $34/$35 minus ($38 + 1), the CLC before SBC taking one extra. Steps back over a literal run plus its control byte, or (with $38 = 1) over a run's value and control byte.

Four words, one per backdrop (index = $AF AND 3): start of each packed bitmap, read by $17BB. The first word at each start is the packed length, added to give the end where unpacking begins: $3F5F-$4AAD (0, Fuji with pagoda and torii), $4AAE-$54AB (1, lake), $54AC-$5CEB (2, dojo), $5CEC-$68CA (3, Buddha). Each unpacks to the 3840 bytes $E640-$F53F, character rows 5-16 of the bitmap at $E000.
High byte of backdrop 0's entry in the bitmap pointer table at $1839, read by $17C6 (the table is read as two interleaved byte tables).

Four words, one per backdrop: start of each nibble-packed colour stream read by $1849: $68CB (Fuji), $6B41 (lake), $6D96 (dojo), $6FE0 (Buddha). Each stream holds three passes: colour RAM $D8C8-$DAA7, then the high and the low nibbles of screen $CCC8-$CEA7 (the bitmap's colours for rows 5-16).
High byte of backdrop 0's entry in the colour pointer table at $1841, read by $1854 (the table is read as two interleaved byte tables).

Unpacks the colours of backdrop ($AF AND 3) from the stream named in $1841. Pass 1 writes low nibbles into colour RAM from $D8C8 (mask $43 = $F0), pass 2 the high nibbles of screen RAM from $CCC8 ($43 = $0F), pass 3 the low nibbles of the same cells ($43 = $F0). Each pass is $188B and ends at a zero count. Uses $3F/$40 source, $41 nibble, $42 read mask, $43 write mask, $36/$37 destination. Called by $1F3A.

One pass of the colour unpacker: reads a control nibble; its bits 0-2 are a count (0 ends the pass). Bit 3 clear: the next count nibbles are literal values. Bit 3 set: the next nibble is repeated count times. Each value goes through $18CB into ($36) under mask $43. No bound on the destination: the stream decides where a pass stops.

Reads the next nibble of the colour stream at ($3F) into A and $41: the low nibble first (mask $42 = $0F), then the high nibble, after which the pointer $3F/$40 advances to the next byte. $42 alternates $0F/$F0.
Writes nibble $41 into ($36) keeping the bits selected by mask $43: $43 = $F0 writes the low nibble, $43 = $0F shifts the value up and writes the high nibble. Advances $36/$37 by one.

Machine set-up, called once from the entry at $1AED. Clears $CF (sound effects on), $FF (no tune), $24, $5D and $C6 (joystick control); installs the interrupt vectors ($1943); copies $C700-$C8FF, where the loader left it, to $0200-$03FF (a 512-byte table of rising values, its use not read here); sets up the VIC and screen ($1991); seeds the random byte $99 with $53 and sets $B6 = 1, the backdrop taken to be in the bitmap, so the first $1F3A with backdrop 0 unpacks it.
Colour RAM $D800-$D8C7 (text rows 0-4, the score panel) set to 6, blue.
Screen $CC00-$CCC7 (text rows 0-4, the score panel) filled with spaces ($20).

Fills colour RAM $DAA8-$DBFF and screen $CEA8-$CFFF with $77: the bitmap colours of character rows 17-24, the strip below the part each backdrop redraws (rows 5-16). The overlapping 256-byte loops also overwrite the sprite pointers at $CFF8-$CFFF.

Interrupt set-up: $01 = 7, CIA 1 interrupts off ($DC0D = $7F), CLI/SEI to take any pending one, VIC raster interrupt enabled ($D01A = 1), $01 = 5 (RAM at $A000 and $E000, I/O at $D000, KERNAL out). Hardware vectors: IRQ $31F2, RESET $1990 (an RTI), NMI $2FF2. CIA 2: all interrupts off, then $DD0D = $82 enables its timer B interrupt (the NMI), timer B latch $DD06/$DD07 = $16BC. CIA 1 port A direction $DC02 = 0. The timer is not started here.

An RTI, installed as the RESET vector at $FFFC by $1943. A real reset restores the ROM banking and takes the KERNAL's vector, so this is only reached by a jump through $FFFC in RAM; nothing in the game was found to do that.

VIC and screen set-up: $DD00 = 0 (VIC bank 3, $C000-$FFFF), $D018 = $38 (screen $CC00, bitmap and font at $E000), blank sprite block 0 ($1AF4), background 1 white, border 3 cyan, $AD = 3, $D011 = $3B (bitmap), raster compare $FF, $D016 = $18 (multicolour), sprite multicolours $D025 = 0 and $D026 = $0A, $22 = 1 and $23 = 2, all sprites multicolour, sprites 0-5 on; colours the bottom strip ($192F), the panel ($1915), clears the panel ($1922); $D022 = 0, $D023 = 1; colour 14 (light blue) for the sixteen yin-yang cells (rows 0-1, columns 3-4, 6-7, 32-33, 35-36).

Puts both fighters at their starting state for an exchange: $6A = $3E and $6B = $5A, $6C/$6D = $50, $45/$46 = $17, $54 = 1, $4B, $4C, $53, $47, $48 and $5E (the knock-down result) cleared; per fighter $1A6F; $76 = 0, $77 = 2, $23 = 2, $86/$87 = 8; then $2593 for each fighter. Called by $1A7C.
Per-fighter reset, X = 0 or 1: $5F,X, $67,X and $74,X cleared, move $61,X = $17.

Runs one exchange of a bout, frame by frame, until it ends; shared by the attract mode and both game modes. Sets $5D = 0, $1A22, $37BD per fighter, CLI, sprites 0-5 on. Each frame (raster line $FD or later): $2808 for fighter 1 then fighter 0 ($69 = 0, 1), $1AFF (random), $1E64 (keys). Returns: minus if $1E64 did (F1 or fire in the attract mode); $5E if non-zero (set at $2A9B when a fighter's knock-down animation ends, from its $5F,X); A = 1 when the clock has run out ($BC), after resetting both fighters with $3914. The clock ($212F) ticks only while $5F and $60 are both zero and fighter 0's move $61 is not $17.
Entry from the loader (SYS 6893, through BASIC's SYS): machine set-up ($18E8), then the outer loop at $1EE1. Never returns.
A lone $60 (RTS) after the entry's JMP; no reference to it was found (opcodes.py --refs $1AF3).
Zeroes $C000-$C03E, sprite shape block 0 of VIC bank 3: a blank sprite. Called by $1991.

Advances the random byte $99 one step: shift left, EOR $1D on carry (an 8-bit Galois shift register, never 0 once seeded). Called once per frame by $1A7C, so $99 depends on how many frames have passed; $1BA7 and $1CD2 copy it into $98, the generator stepped by $2589.

Two-player game, chosen by $AE = 1. Backdrop $AF = 0, $65 and $66 = 0 (neither fighter computer-controlled), panel text cleared ($21A5, $227F), yin-yang cells cleared, $B0 = 1 (a game is running), score fields reset ($1F5D), tune $FF = 3. Four bouts, one per backdrop, each of 30 clock units ($B1 = 50 passes, $B2 = 30, $217B shows 30) through $1B7A, with a pause of 15 x 6 frames ($21C8) between. Then compares the scores ($1F74): equal, both fighters' end animation ($1E44); else the judge signals the winner ($1F93, $1E32). High-score check ($200A), a pause, A = 0. A minus result from a bout returns minus, and $1EE1 starts the game again.

One two-player bout: exchanges ($1A7C) until the clock runs out ($BC). After each knock-down, when exactly one fighter has bit 4 of $5F,X set, the other's score goes up ($206C: X = 9 player 1's field when $5F = 0, X = $19 player 2's otherwise). Yin-yang cells are cleared after every exchange: in this mode only points count, and no score of symbols ends a bout early. Returns minus if $1A7C does.

One-player game, chosen by $AE = 0. $CA, backdrop $AF and rank $B4 = 0, $65 = 0 (fighter 0 the player) and $66 = 1 (fighter 1 the computer), $B0 = 1, $B5 = 2, score fields reset, $98 seeded from $99, NOVICE written at $CCA0 ($21FB), tune $FF = 2. Each bout: clear symbols, 30-unit clock, backdrop ($1F3A), $1C72. A won bout decrements $B5: two wins clear a rank, after which, when $AF AND 3 is 3 (the Buddha backdrop), $132C runs; then below $AF = 10 the rank $B4 and $AF go up and the new rank is written (1ST DAN ... 10TH DAN). Past that, $1C5B. A draw ($81) plays both end animations and repeats the bout; a lost bout or a minus result ends the game: high-score check ($200A), panel text ($2115), A = 0.

After the tenth-dan rank is cleared: $AF = ((AF + 1) AND 3) OR $20, so the backdrops keep cycling and $AF stays at 10 or more, and $B4, the opponent's level, becomes a random 7 to 10 ($2589). The rank text is not rewritten, so it keeps reading 10TH DAN whatever $B4 is.

One one-player bout: exchanges ($1A7C) until a fighter has two whole yin-yangs or the clock runs out. When fighter 1 is knocked down (exactly one fighter with bit 4 of $5F,X, and $5F = 0) the player scores points ($206C X = 9), $BD gains ($2169) and $1D5F adds to $8A; when fighter 0 is, the computer gains $BE and $8B. Four halves win: the player's win runs down the clock for a bonus ($21DF) and returns 1; the computer's returns 0. At time-up the more half-symbols ($8A against $8B) wins, then the more points ($BD against $BE), the judge signalling ($1F93); a full tie returns $81. Returns minus if $1A7C does.

The attract mode: the computer fights itself under DEMO. $AF = 0, $98 from $99, levels $B3 and $B4 random 3 to 11 (rand AND 7, + 3 + carry), panel cleared, DEMO written ($21B3), $65 = $66 = 1 (both fighters computer-controlled), tune $FF = 1, $04F0 = $FF. One 30-unit demo bout ($1D33) on each of the four backdrops in turn. Returns plus after the fourth, and $1EE1 starts it over; returns minus when F1 or fire was pressed, and $1EE1 starts a game.

One attract-mode bout: exchanges ($1A7C) until a fighter has two whole yin-yangs ($1D5F, then that fighter's end animation $1E32) or the clock runs out. No points are scored. Returns 0, or minus if $1A7C does.

Adds the value of the blow just landed, $6E,X (1 = half, 2 = whole), to fighter X's count of halves $8A,X and redraws that fighter's symbols: 1 a half, 2 one whole, 3 a whole and a half, 4 or more two wholes. Fighter 0's sit at panel columns 6 and 3, fighter 1's at 32 and 35 (Y = 3/0 and $1D/$20). Returns carry set when the count has reached 4: the bout is won.
Draws a whole yin-yang, characters $21-$24 in a 2 x 2 block at $CC03,Y (rows 0-1). Called by $1D5F and from $2C2B.
Draws a half yin-yang, characters $25-$28 in a 2 x 2 block at $CC03,Y. Called by $1D5F and from $2C3E.
Clears one fighter's two yin-yang blocks (spaces at $CC03/$CC04/$CC06/$CC07 and the row below, offset by Y): Y = 0 fighter 0, Y = $1D fighter 1.
Puts fighter X in the pose $45,X = $19, with $6C,X = $50 and $47,X, $4B,X cleared: the start of the end-of-bout animation that $1E32 and $1E44 play out.
Fighter X's end-of-bout animation ($1E23) played frame by frame with $37BD until its finished flag $59,X is set. Used for the winner of a bout.
Both fighters' end-of-bout animation ($1E23 for each), stepped with $37BD each frame until fighter 1's $59,X is set. Used for a drawn bout.

Reads keyboard row 0 (CIA 1: $DC00 = $FE, $DC01) and acts when it differs from last time ($BB): F1 ($EF) returns $80; F3 ($DF) flips players $AE between 0 and 1 and redraws the panel ($2186, $2115); F7 ($F7) flips control $C6 joystick/keyboard ($228A); DEL ($FE) flips the sound-effects flag $CF; F5 ($BF) jumps straight to $1EE1. F1, F3, F7 and DEL count only while $B0 = 0 (the attract mode); F5 always. Otherwise, while $B0 = 0, fire on joystick port 2 ($DC00 bit 4) returns $80. Returns 0 for nothing.

The outer loop, entered from $1AED and from F5 at $1ED1 (a JMP from deep inside the call chain: the stack is not reset). $AE = 0 (one player). Each pass redraws the panel ($2115 high score, $2186 1/2 PLAYER, $228A JOYSTICK/KEYBOARD), $B0 = 0, clears both score fields, and runs the attract mode $1CD2 until it returns minus (F1 or fire). Then $AE = 0: the one-player game $1BA7 followed by $146A and $16E6; $AE = 1: the two-player game $1B09, repeated while it returns minus.

Clears $E640-$F53F, the 15 pages of bitmap that each backdrop redraws (character rows 5-16). It writes the STA's address operand at $1F2E/$1F2F to $E640 first, then steps its high byte, so after a run the operand reads $F540.
Low byte of the STA operand at $1F2D, written ($40) by $1F1E.
High byte of the STA operand at $1F2D, written ($E6) and stepped by $1F1E.

Turns sprites 6 and 7 off ($D015 = $3F) and, when backdrop ($AF AND 3) is not the one in the bitmap ($B6), draws it: $2FEC = 3, clear ($1F1E), colours ($1849), bitmap ($17BB), $2FEC = 1. The backdrops are packed in memory; no disk access.
Resets a six-digit score field on text row 1 to blanks and a final 0: X = 9 player 1 (columns 9-14), X = $19 player 2 (columns 25-30).
Compares the two score fields digit by digit ($CC31 against $CC41, six characters). X = 0 when player 1's is higher, 1 when player 2's is, $80 when equal (N set).

Shows the judge's decision for fighter X with sprites 6 and 7: sprite 6 colour 12, pointer from $1FFA (shape $5C for backdrops 0 and 1, where the judge sits on the right, $50 for 2 and 3), position from $1FFE, $2002, $2006; sprite 7, pointer $51, a small shape in colour X + 1 (1 white for fighter 0, 2 red for fighter 1), placed beside it. Then sprites 6 and 7 on.
Sprite 6 pointer per backdrop for $1F93: $5C, $5C, $50, $50.
Sprite 6 X position, low byte, per backdrop for $1F93; four bytes running to $2001 ($12, $20, $58, $46), the high bits at $2002.
Per-backdrop bits 6-7 of $D010 (X bit 8 of sprites 6 and 7), indexed by $AF AND 3 at $1FBA: $C0,$C0,$00,$00. Read only there.
Per-backdrop Y position of sprite 6 ($D00D), indexed by $AF AND 3 at $1FC0: $9E,$99,$94,$96; sprite 7's Y is derived from it at $1FD6. Read only there.

Copies a player's score into the high score of the current mode when it is higher. $AE=0 (one player): table $1299, score at $CC31. $AE<>0 (two players): table $129F, X=0 player 1's score ($CC31), else player 2's ($CC41). Uses $BF/$C0 as the table pointer; X destroyed.

Compares the 6 screen-code digits at ($BF) (a stored high score) with the 6 on screen at $CC28+X, most significant first. Returns C clear when the screen number is the larger, C set when it is equal or smaller. Spaces ($20) sort below digits.
Copies the 6 characters on screen at $CC28+X to ($BF),0..5: stores a new high score.

Adds a blow's award to a player's on-screen score: $12A5[$8C] hundreds, $8C being the attacker's move (stored at $2CAC), halved unless the blow was a whole symbol ($6E for X=9, $6F otherwise; 2 whole, 1 half, set at $2C20/$2C33). Calls score_add_100 that many times; a blank tens digit becomes '0' first. X = 9 for the score at $CC31, $19 for $CC41. An award of 0 would add 25600 (Y wraps).

Adds 100 to the six-digit decimal score drawn on screen at $CC28+X..$CC2D+X (screen codes, $30-$39, leading blanks $20). Increments the hundreds digit at $CC2B+X and carries leftward; a blank digit becomes '1'. Past 999999 all six digits become '0'.

Draws the high score of the current mode in the top panel: 6 characters from $1299 ($AE=0, one player) or $129F (two players) to $CCB1. Called each pass of the outer loop at $1EE5 and from $1C55, $1EBB. Not per-fighter work.

Bout clock. Every 50 calls ($B1 counts down from $32) takes one unit off the two-digit clock on screen at $CC3B/$CC3C (tens blanked below 10) and decrements $B2 (30 at $1B37); when $B2 reaches 0 sets $BC=1, time up. Called from $1AC7 and the time bonus loop. (Measured live: the clock counts passes of the exchange loop, not frames. A unit took 50 PAL frames, one second, with the computer fighting, and 60-66 frames with two idle players, so a 30-unit bout lasts about 30 to 40 seconds.)

Adds a blow's value $12A5[$8C], halved unless $6E is 2, to fighter X's tally $BD,X. Reads $6E, fighter 0's whole/half flag, for both fighters, where score_add_award uses $6F for the second: a slip, or deliberate. Called from $1C85 (X=1) and $1C97 (X=0).
Writes '30' into the clock digits on screen at $CC3B/$CC3C. Called at bout start from $1B3F, $1C07, $1D1F.

Draws the player count in the top panel at $CCBF: the 8 characters '1 PLAYER' ($12BE) when $AE=0, '2 PLAYER' ($12C6) when $AE=1, nothing for other values. Called from the outer loop at $1EE8 and from $1EB8.
Blanks the two 8-character panel fields at $CCA0 (rank or DEMO) and $CC97 (JOYSTICK/KEYBOARD) with spaces. Called from $1B11, $1BB1.
Writes DEMO ($44 $45 $4D $4F, immediates) at $CCA0, the rank field. Called from $1CEF when the attract-mode fight is set up.
Delay: X times six passes of the raster beam over line $FE, so about X*6 frames. Uses Y; X ends 0. Called from $1B54, $1B74, $21F3.
Delay entry used from $1778: waits for Y passes of raster line $FE (each pass: wait for line $FE, then for it to end). Falls into the X loop of wait_6x_frames, so the caller's X counts too.

End-of-bout time bonus, if the clock has not run out ($BC=0): runs bout_clock_tick until each unit ticks over, adds 100 to player 1's score ($CC31, X=9) per unit left, pauses about 6 frames each, until $BC is set. Called from $1CBE.

Writes a rank name through ($BF): X=0 'NOVICE ' (7 bytes from $22B4) at offset 2*$CA; X=1..9 the digit, 'ST'/'ND'/'RD'/'TH' and ' DAN' at offset $CA; X=10 '10TH DAN' ($22BB) at offset 0. Called from $1C40 with X from level_rank_table, and from $15DE, $1BE0.
Blanks the 8-character rank field at $CCA0 with spaces. Called from $1B14, $1BB4, $1CEC.
Draws the control mode in the top panel at $CC97: 'JOYSTICK' when $C6=0, 'KEYBOARD' otherwise. Called from the outer loop at $1EEB and from $1ECB (the F7 toggle).
'JOYSTICK', 8 codes in the game's ASCII-ordered font ($41='A'), copied by panel_show_controls.
'KEYBOARD', 8 font codes, copied by panel_show_controls when $C6 is set.
'NOVICE ' with a trailing space, 7 font codes, copied by rank_text_draw for rank 0.
'10TH DAN', 8 font codes, copied by rank_text_draw for rank 10. Ranks 1-9 are built from immediates instead.
Displayed rank for each opponent level $B4: 0,1,2,..,10,10 (12 entries, levels 0-11). Read at $1C3B to pick the text rank_text_draw shows.

Computer opponent, once per call for fighter X (Y=$69 the other fighter); reached by JMP from $2849 when $65,X is set (computer-controlled) and $5F,X is clear. Output: the requested move $63,X, normally the held choice $90,X. Order: opponent in a forced move ($5F,opp) -> stand when own move is $0E, else count $A1,X down and stand at 0; a plan in progress ($9D,X) -> ai_plan_dispatch; opponent attacking ($1176[$61,opp]<>0) -> block, hold or counter; otherwise ai_no_threat.

Opponent attacking while this fighter stands or walks (move 1-3). $2D00 decides whether the attack is in range; if not, ai_no_threat. Then a reaction delay: $AA,X counts down a start value of random AND $AC (per level, none from level 4). Then random AND $9C: bit 7 counter-attacks (ai_choose_attack), bits 4-6 block with $118F[opponent move], low nibble 0 picks move 9 or $0B at random, otherwise starts the plan $2788[opponent move] in $9D,X (or blocks when that is 0).

No attack to answer. While $4B,X is set the held move stays. While $74,X is set: a turn-round (move $12) with $9A,X set ends by flipping facing $53,X and standing; other moves are held for a random time ($8E,X = random AND $8D + 5) then dropped to stand. Otherwise, from moves 1-3, measures the distance (ai_measure); any other move is held.

Distance to the opponent into $73, signed along this fighter's facing. Facing each other: far ahead ($15-$7F) approach, behind ($80-$D4) turn round, close ($D5-$14) ai_close_range. Same facing: close is $DF-$1E, $1F-$7F (opponent behind) turns, $80-$DE approaches.

Opponent out of reach ahead: when the pause counter $A4,X runs out, walk forward (move 2) for random AND $A8,X calls; while already walking, stop (move 1) for random AND $A6,X calls when that is non-zero. Both masks come from the opponent level.
Requests move $12 and sets $9A,X so that ai_no_threat flips the facing when it ends. Used when the opponent is behind, and as one outcome of ai_back_attack.

Opponent within reach: hesitate first. $95,X negative loads random AND $97 (per level) and stands; positive counts down while standing; at zero it is reset to $80 and the fighter attacks (ai_choose_attack).

Picks an attack. Same facing -> ai_attack_behind. Opponent in move $13 -> $27A1[random AND 3]; in move $14 -> $27A5[random AND 3] (7 there starts plan 5). Otherwise $26D5[$73+$33 + random AND $94], adjusted: $0E becomes walk forward (2) from level 7; $0A is skipped below level 2; 7 starts plan 5; $0F/$10 go to ai_back_attack; others through ai_lower_if_opponent_low.
JMP $2415, unreachable: the RTS at $251D precedes it and nothing branches or jumps here (opcodes.py --refs, cross-references). Left over from an edit.
Requests move 4 and sets plan 5 in $9D,X, so that the next calls go through ai_plan_crouch_spring.
Attack choice when both fighters face the same way: move $2725[$73+$29 + random AND $94], through ai_lower_if_opponent_low; $0F and $10 go to ai_back_attack.
For moves $0F/$10: random AND $A3 (per level). Bit 7 turns round instead; $40-$7F walks back (move 3); $20-$3F uses move 8; below $20 keeps the move.

Random number: $98 shifted left, XOR $1D when a bit falls out (polynomial $11D, all 255 non-zero values in turn; a 0 seed would stay 0). Returns the new $98 in A with N and Z set from it. Seeded from $99 at $1BD2 and $1CD8.

Loads the computer's parameters for fighter X from its level $B3,X (0-11): per fighter $A8,X ($27CD) $A6,X ($27D8) $AA,X=$80; shared, so the last call (X=1) wins: $8D/$A1/$A2 ($27A9), $94 ($27B5), $A3 ($27E4), $97 ($27C1), $9C ($27F0), $AC ($27FC). Resets both fighters' $8E,$90,$95,$9A,$9D,$A4. Called from $1A66 (X=0) and $1A6B (X=1).
Plan 1: crouch (move 4) until an opening, then strike with move $0A and end the plan. Below level 7 the opening is the opponent standing (move 1); from level 7 it is the opponent's $51 being $19.
Plan 3: requests move $0E once and ends the plan ($9D,X=0).
Plan 4: requests move 9 once and ends the plan ($9D,X=0).
Plan 5: holds move 4 (crouch) until $74,X is set, then requests move 7 and ends the plan.
Plan 8: at random either goes to plan 6, or sets $9D=5 and runs plan 5. The store is $9D without X, fighter 0's plan, whichever fighter is thinking.
Plan 6: requests move 6 or move $18 at random and ends the plan.

Plan 7: requests $0A when $53,X equals $0053+Y, else $10, and ends the plan. Y is 14 here (the plan number doubled at $2689), so it compares facing with $61, fighter 0's move: probably meant LDY $69 and the opponent's facing.
Plan 2: requests move $0A until the fighter is in it, then ends the plan.
Runs the plan in progress: A = $9D,X (1-9) indexes the word table ai_plan_handlers, through $9F/$A0 and JMP ($9F). Y is left as A*2.
A = a chosen move. When the opponent's move is $0A, $10, 4 or 7 (the low ones), returns $12D0[A] instead (the low counterpart of an attack); otherwise returns A. Uses $CE as scratch.
Plan 9: from level 7, half the time requests move $0D and ends the plan; otherwise switches to plan 1 and runs it.

80 moves: the attack against an opponent with the opposite facing, indexed by $73+$33 plus random AND $94 ($24F8); $73 is $D5-$14 there, so indexes $08-$4E (the first 8 bytes are never read). Opponent behind, back to back: mostly $0F/$10 (fire with up or down and back on the stick); just behind: walks; just ahead: $18, 6, 7, $11, $0D; a little further: $0E, $0C, $0A, $0B; beyond: stand or walk.

79 moves: the attack when both face the same way, indexed by $73+$29 plus random AND $94 ($2554); $73 is $DF-$1E there, so indexes $08-$4E end at $2773. Opponent ahead with its back turned: $0A, $0E, $0C, $0B, $11, $0D, $18, 6; close either side: walks; opponent behind: $0F, then $10 further off.

Ten words, the plan handlers for $9D,X = 0-9 (0 unused, $0000): ai_plan_crouch_wait, ai_plan_move_0a, ai_plan_move_0e, ai_plan_move_09, ai_plan_crouch_spring, ai_plan_move_06_or_18, ai_plan_0a_or_10, ai_plan_mixed, ai_plan_level_choice. Read at $268B/$2690.
High bytes of the ai_plan_handlers words, read separately by the LDA $2775,Y at $2690.
Plan to start in answer to each opponent move 0-$18 ($23A4): 6->8, 7->2, $0A->4, $0B->3, $0C->2, $0E->9, $0F->4, $10->7, $11->2, others 0 (block instead).
Attacks against an opponent in move $13: 6, $0D, $0E, $11, picked by random AND 3 at $24E0. These are the moves whose block ($118F) is $14, not $13.
Attacks against an opponent in move $14: 7, $0B, $0C, $18, picked by random AND 3 at $24CE (7 starts plan 5). Their block in $118F is $13.
Per level 0-11 into $8D, $A1, $A2: 1F 1F 0F 0F 0F 0F 07 07.. ; $8D masks the random hold time in ai_no_threat, $A1,X is the wait while the opponent is in a forced move.
Per level into $94: 7 for levels 0-4, 3 from 5. Masks the random offset into the attack tables, so higher levels pick from fewer, nearer entries.
Per level into $97: 7F 1F 0F 0F 0F 07 7F 1F 07 0F 3F 1F. Masks the hesitation at close range (ai_close_range) before an attack.
Per level into $A8,X: masks how long ai_approach walks forward. 11 bytes; level 11 reads $27D8, the next table's first byte.
Per level into $A6,X: masks the pause ai_approach makes while walking; 0 (level 7) means it never pauses.
Per level into $A3: masks the random value of ai_back_attack (bit 7 turn, $40 walk back, $20 move 8). Byte-identical with Fist II's opponent style data (brief, mapf2.py).

Per level into $9C: masks the response roll in ai_threat_in_range (bit 7 counter-attack, bits 4-6 block, low nibble plan): A3 B2 F1 F0 70 8F 7F 0F 7F 7F 7F 7F. Levels 4 and 6-11 have bit 7 clear and never counter-attack outright; level 4 ($70) always blocks.
Per level into $AC: 1F 0F 07 03 for levels 0-3, mask of the reaction delay before answering an attack. Levels 4-11 read $2800-$2807, all 0: no delay.

Entries 4-11 of the 12-byte per-rank table that starts at $27FC (agent 4's range): $1F $0F $07 $03 at $27FC-$27FF, then eight zeros here. Read only by LDA $27FC,Y at $25E2 (Y = 0-11, the table stride of the set-up at $2595-$25E7), which copies the byte to $AC. What $AC does is not traced here.

Per-frame update of fighter X (0 or 1; $69 holds the other one). Called twice from $1AA3/$1AAA, fighter 1 first. In order: $2B70 hit test on the attack's striking frame, $2834 read the control (stick, keys, computer or forced move) into the request $63,X, $2AF2 turn a pull-back into a block, $29B4 choose the next move $61,X from the request, $2B46 start or hold its animation, $2A8F handle the end of the animation. Then reads the sprite-sprite collision register $D01E (which clears it) and, if any of sprites 0-2 has touched another sprite, sets $24 (which fighter is drawn with sprites 0-2, read at $3220): X when fighter X is in an attack move ($1176,Y non-zero), the opponent $69 when fighter X is in move $11.

Fills the request $63,X for fighter X. A forced move in $5F,X (the hit reactions $16/$1A/$1B written at $2CD9-$2CEF) wins; otherwise $65,X non-zero hands over to the computer opponent at $22CF; otherwise $C6 non-zero reads the keyboard ($288C), zero the joystick ($284C). Also called alone from $12FC.

Joystick for fighter X: sets CIA 1 port A to input ($DC02 = 0) and reads $DC00,X, so fighter 0 reads port A (joystick port 2) and fighter 1 port B $DC01 (joystick port 1). Keeps bits 0-4 (up, down, left, right, fire; active low) and falls into the decoder.

Turns a 5-bit stick value in A (bits 0-4 up/down/left/right/fire, active low; the keyboard routines build the same value) into a move request. When the facing $53,X is non-zero and left or right is pressed (but not both), left and right are swapped (EOR #$0C), so the table reads them relative to the facing. Then $63,X = joy_move_table[value].

Move requested for each stick value, 32 bytes indexed by bits 0-4 of the port (active low; $00-$0F with fire, $10-$1F without), left/right as read with facing $53,X = 0. Without fire: none 1, up 5, down 4, left 3, right 2, up-left 9, up-right 6, down-left 8, down-right 7. With fire: fire alone 1, up $0E, down $0A, left $11, right $0C, up-left $0F, up-right $0D, down-left $10, down-right $0B. Opposite directions held together give 1. Sixteen moves plus 1 (no request).

Keyboard control for fighter X: port A all outputs, port B all inputs ($DC02 = $FF, $DC03 = 0). Fighter 0 uses $28B2 (fire) and $28CA (direction), fighter 1 $2931 and $2953. The direction code (a joystick-style low nibble, active low) plus the fire bit in $C5 ($10 = no fire, 0 = fire) is passed to the stick decoder $2856, so the keys emulate a joystick.
Fire key for keyboard player 1 (fighter 0): keyboard row 1 ($DC00 = $FD), columns 5 and 7 (S and left SHIFT). Either held: $C5 = 0; neither: $C5 = $10 (the joystick's fire bit, active low).

Direction keys for keyboard player 1 (fighter 0), returned in A as a joystick nibble (bits 0-3 up/down/left/right, active low). Tested in this order, the first held key wins: Q up-left ($0A), E up-right ($06), Z down-left ($09), W up ($0E), C down-right ($05), X down ($0D), D right ($07), A left ($0B); none $0F. The eight keys ring S, which is a fire key ($28B2). $C4 is scratch.
Fire key for keyboard player 2 (fighter 1): right SHIFT (row 6 column 4) or : (row 5 column 5). Either held: $C5 = 0; neither: $C5 = $10.

Direction keys for keyboard player 2 (fighter 1), as a joystick nibble in A, first held key wins: / down-right ($05), * up-right ($06), P up-left ($0A), @ up ($0E), comma down-left ($09), full stop down ($0D), L left ($0B), ; right ($07); none $0F. The eight keys ring :, which is a fire key ($2931). $C4 is scratch.

Chooses fighter X's move $61,X from the request $63,X. Hit reactions $16/$1A/$1B: wait while the counter $86,X runs down (holding, $74,X = 1), then take the move with height $6C,X = $50, $74 and $4B cleared, and the sample started at $316A if $88,X is set and the pose $51,X is $28 or $2C.
